name: Hereditary Pancreatitis

criteria.description: Recurrent acute pancreatitis (2 or more episodes) with onset before age 20
Pathogenic variant in PRSS1 gene (most common: R122H, N29I)
Family history of pancreatitis in 2 or more first-degree relatives across 2 generations
Chronic pancreatitis developing at young age (< 25 years)
Pathogenic variants in SPINK1, CFTR, or CTRC genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Either (1) pathogenic PRSS1 mutation, or (2) family history of pancreatitis in >= 2 first-degree relatives in >= 2 generations with early-onset recurrent pancreatitis. Genetic testing confirms diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: PRSS1 mutations account for ~80% of genetically confirmed hereditary pancreatitis. SPINK1, CFTR, CTRC mutations may contribute as susceptibility factors.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent episodes of acute pancreatitis beginning in childhood
pathognomonic.notes: First attack often before age 10; recurrences throughout life

common.symptomName: Severe epigastric pain radiating to back

occasional.notes: Pancreatogenic diabetes from progressive gland destruction

rare.notes: Lifetime risk ~40% by age 70; dramatically elevated compared to general population

laboratory: Elevated serum lipase/amylase during acute attacks
Fecal elastase-1 low (< 200 mcg/g) in chronic pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency
HbA1c elevated if pancreatogenic diabetes develops
Elevated IgG4 should be checked to exclude autoimmune pancreatitis
imaging: CT abdomen: pancreatic calcifications, ductal dilation, parenchymal atrophy in chronic disease
EUS: parenchymal and ductal changes of chronic pancreatitis
genetic: PRSS1 gene mutations: R122H (most common), N29I, A16V (autosomal dominant, ~80% penetrance)
SPINK1 gene mutations: N34S (recessive susceptibility factor)
CFTR gene mutations: may act as modifier/susceptibility gene
other: Secretin-stimulated MRCP for early chronic pancreatitis
Endoscopic ultrasound with Rosemont criteria for chronic pancreatitis
Pancreatic cancer screening recommended starting age 40 (or 20 years after first attack)

distinguishingFeatures: Alcoholic pancreatitis has significant alcohol use history
CF has pulmonary disease, elevated sweat chloride
CF confirmed by CFTR mutation analysis and sweat test

redFlags: New-onset diabetes, weight loss, or jaundice in chronic pancreatitis (screen for pancreatic cancer)
Severe necrotizing pancreatitis requiring ICU care
Development of pancreatic mass lesion on surveillance imaging
references: Whitcomb DC, et al. Hereditary pancreatitis is caused by a mutation in the cationic trypsinogen gene. Nat Genet. 1996;14(2):141-145.
Rebours V, et al. The natural history of hereditary pancreatitis: a national series. Gut. 2009;58(1):97-103.
Shelton C, et al. Hereditary Pancreatitis. GeneReviews. 2023.
